To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) responsiveness of software can be defined in a manner that is consistent across all levels of the software life cycle, (b) responsiveness of software systems can be improved by applying general principles that are independent of specific software systems, (c) the general principles are based on the interrelationships between two models, a software model and a computer system model, that are used to predict performance, and (d) the performance effect of each principle is quantified using these two models. 1
the three principles, when applied in software design, lead to software that is responsive, maintainable, and understandable.

responsiveness is best achieved by: (1) minimizing the number of software components, (2) minimizing the amount of work done in each component, and (3) maximizing the degree to which software components can be overlapped.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of general principles that will lead to the construction of software that is responsive, understandable, maintainable, and cost-effective.
the construction of software systems with acceptable performance.
the development of a methodology for the construction of responsive software systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the three general principles for responsive software design are: (1) minimize the number of software components, (2) minimize the number and length of software paths, and (3) maximize the number of software paths that are used.
the principles should be used to define the requirements and design of software systems that have to be responsive.
the three principles are necessary and sufficient to achieve responsive software systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a set of general software performance principles that are independent of the application domain and can be applied in the early software life cycle phases.
the three general principles are independent and are not in conflict with each other.

the principles are useful in the early life cycle stages for defining software requirements and designs that are responsive, maintainable, and understandable, and that they are applicable for both real time and non-real-time software systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the principles are general, can be applied to a variety of system designs, and can be used to improve the quality of the design and the responsiveness of the software system.
software responsiveness is an important system property that must be considered early in the software development life cycle.
the three general principles are applicable in early software life-cycle stages for the definition and design of software systems with acceptable performance.
